observations: Photo 0 shows a blue and black bicycle with a visible brand name 'Giant' on the frame.
Photo 1 shows a red and black bicycle with the brand name 'Redman' visible on the frame.
Photo 2 is a duplicate of Photo 0, showing the same blue and black bicycle.
Both bicycles have 26-inch wheels, front suspension forks, and appear to be mountain-style bikes.
The blue bicycle has a black saddle and a rear fender; the red bicycle has a brown saddle and a rear fender.
Both bikes are standing on kickstands on a paved brick surface.
The background in all photos shows an outdoor market or yard with other items and people visible.

claims.evidence: Both bicycles appear clean and in good condition with no visible damage or excessive wear in the photos.

risks.risk: Internal frame damage or rust not visible in photos

risks.risk: Brakes or gears not functioning properly
risks.proof: Video clip showing the brakes being applied and the gears shifting through all ratios.

risks.risk: Tires worn beyond safe tread depth
risks.proof: Close-up shot of the tire treads on both front and rear wheels.

risks.risk: Chain or drivetrain rust or damage
risks.proof: Close-up shot of the chain, cassette, and chainring.

proof_requests: Video clip showing brakes and gears in operation.
Close-up photos of frame joints and welds.
Close-up photo of chain and drivetrain.
response.reason: The bicycles are identifiable by brand and appear neat, but critical functional and structural aspects like brakes, gears, frame integrity, and tire condition cannot be verified from current photos. These risks affect pricing and must be proven before a final price can be assigned.
